html:
A customs official born on Goree who in 1914 became the first black African elected to the French Chamber of Deputies, for the Four Communes of Senegal.

In 1916 he got a law passed confirming that the Africans of the Four Communes were French citizens. In 1918 France sent him to recruit soldiers in West Africa, promising rights in return, and he raised some 60,000 men for the Tirailleurs. Later he defended French colonial labour policy at the International Labour Organization, which angered many. He was mayor of Dakar and served in the French government. Dakar's international airport bears his name.
